claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I need to ask you some questions about your situation.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 17 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask you a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in school, college, sixth form, or an approved training program?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. He finished his GCSEs and left education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to understand Alex's current situation a bit better.

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't signed up with the careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I need to ask a few more questions to complete my assessment.

**Is Alex currently working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that - I don't know if he's claiming any benefits himself.

Based on the information you've provided, I cannot make a definitive determination about your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex at this time.

**Here's the situation:**

Alex is 17 and has left education without being in approved training. For Child Benefit to continue for 16-19 year olds, they normally need to be in approved education or training. 

There is a provision where Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services after leaving education - but Alex hasn't done this.

Additionally, Child Benefit stops if a child starts claiming certain benefits in their own right (like Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit). Since you're unsure whether Alex is claiming any benefits himself, I cannot make a definitive assessment.

**What you should do:**

1. **Find out if Alex is claiming any benefits in his own right** - you can ask him directly or check any correspondence he may have received
2. **Contact the Child Benefit Office** directly at HMRC - they can check Alex's status and give you a definitive answer about your entitlement

They'll be able to access the information needed to determine whether you're still entitled to Child Benefit for Alex.
